field_check.governing_thought: Computer science divides by the property asserted of a computation, ordered from the single program outward to many agents and adversaries: correctness, cost, coordination, learning, and protection.
key_line: Correctness is the property that a computation does what its specification, formal model or mathematical foundation says it should.
Cost is the property of how much time, energy, information capacity or algorithmic effort a computation requires.
Coordination is the property of how a computation cooperates with other components, machines, networks and people.
Learning is the property that a computation improves its behaviour, reasons or acts intelligently from data and experience.
Protection is the property that a computation and its data resist attack, misuse and failure.
field_check.note: P1.3 is a catch-all mixing dependability with General/reference/Document types; P2.3 media/graphics and P3.2 application/human areas are topics, not cost or coordination properties.
